The simple reason is that consumers are unable to maintain consumption. The working person's paycheck has simply been shrinking in purchasing power over the decades to the point now that even major low-price chains find they no longer have the amount of business necessary to keep up profits in order to justify staying open.

The paychecks going to workers are too small and these workers can no longer borrow their way forward.

The situation is desperate and a function of exactly how capitalism is structured.

Business is in business to make a profit. That is logical. Profit is achieved by keeping costs, including labor costs, less than the price that consumers will pay for goods and services. In any individual case, this is just fine as there are many businesses spreading the worker/consumer base. But in the aggregate and over the cycle life of the "game" the workers, as a whole, fall behind. Consumption fails to keep up with production.

And this leads to a vicious cycle of : price lowering-> pay cuts-> layoffs-> less consumption-> less production-> more pay cuts/more job cuts etc etc. Gimmicks like inserting more workers into the workforce (women) and by longer work hours and then by personal debt/borrowing eventually get tapped out.

Today they are tapped out.

In the global macroeconomic picture, this is leading to what we call DEFLATION. In this situation, creating a business makes no sense. Keeping money/capital on the sideline makes risk free money. This is why negative interest rates are starting to be paid out to borrowers in Europe. "Borrow from us to start a business/hold our money and we will PAY YOU!"

Wealth inequality is the final toxic product of any capitalist system that has inadequate social controls. The fix has always been a choice of these three governmental functions: Taxation, Inflation, and/or Confiscation. The money siphoned from the rich must then be funneled back to the worker/consumer to sustain the system.
